rules.title: No-fault eviction relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict (RSO & JCO)
rules.requirement: Before a not-at-fault eviction from a unit covered by the RSO or the JCO, the landlord must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD. Notices to terminate may be served only after the Declaration is filed, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after service. Not-at-fault reasons include occupancy by the landlord, listed family members or a resident manager; demolition, commercial conversion or removal from rental use; a government order to vacate; HUD recovery before sale; residential hotel conversion or demolition; and conversion to affordable housing.
rules.coverage_text: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
rules.exemptions: Relocation assistance is not owed when evicting a resident manager to replace him/her with another resident manager (unless a Manager-Tenant receiving free or reduced rent with no other compensation), or when required to evict due to hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster not caused by the landlord's negligence. A landlord may offset the tenant's accumulated rent against relocation assistance, except where owed because of a governmental order to vacate or an order for an unpermitted dwelling.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO. The tenant may raise the landlord's failure to provide relocation assistance as an affirmative defense in an action to recover possession.
rules.quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.

rules.title: Relocation assistance amounts for no-fault evictions (Chart A)
rules.requirement: Relocation assistance for no-fault evictions is paid per unit and depends on whether the tenant is eligible or qualified, the length of tenancy and income: eligible households $11,000 (less than 3 years) or $14,400 (3 or more years or low income); qualified households $23,150 or $27,400. Qualified tenants are those 62 or older, handicapped or disabled, or with minor dependent children.
rules.key_value: Eligible: $11,000 (<3 years) / $14,400 (3+ years or low income at or below 80% AMI); Qualified: $23,150 / $27,400
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced for a no-fault reason from units under the RSO or JCO; does not apply to lower-income tenants displaced by demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction.
rules.exemptions: The amounts do not apply if the eviction is for demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction and the tenant is lower-income (80% AMI or lower).
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation fees due to the tenant by the landlord depends on whether the tenant is an eligible or qualified tenant, the length of tenancy, and the tenant’s income. Relocation Assistance is paid per unit, not per tenant.

rules.title: Mom and Pop reduced relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Mom and Pop landlords may pay reduced relocation assistance ($10,550 eligible, $21,250 qualified) only for evictions for occupancy by the owner or an eligible relative, if the building has four or fewer rental units, the landlord has not used the provision in the previous three years, the landlord owns no more than four units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City, and the relative owns no residential property in the City.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with four or fewer rental units owned by a landlord owning no more than four units and one single-family home in the City; owner or eligible relative occupancy evictions only.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for single-family dwellings owned by natural persons (JCO)
rules.requirement: For a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO owned by a natural person who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City, relocation assistance is one month's rent in effect when the notice was served, paid as money or credit.
rules.coverage_text: Single-family dwellings subject to the JCO whose owner is a natural person (including via a trust or controlled legal entity) owning no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: When the residential real property  is a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO and the owner is a natural person, including natural  persons who hold properties in a trust or registered legal entity controlled by   that natural person, who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot  in the City of Los Angeles: one month’s rent that was in effect when   the landlord served the written notice to terminate the tenancy, as either a monetary payment or credit.
rules.interaction_text: The Los Angeles Municipal Code Section 151.30(E) shall not apply.

rules.title: Timing and manner of relocation assistance payment
rules.requirement: Relocation assistance must be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction, split pro rata among multiple tenants, with the higher amount paid if more than one applies. The landlord may instead deposit the funds in an escrow account within the 15-day period, with payments made within three (3) working days of a request.

rules.coverage_text: Landlords paying relocation assistance under the RSO or JCO.

rules.title: Eviction for demolition for new construction (Protected Units)
rules.requirement: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict (JCO units) or Notice of Intent to Withdraw (RSO units) with LAHD, serve written notice and file a copy within 3 business days, and pay relocation assistance under the Housing Crisis Act or City law, whichever is higher, with RSO/JCO amounts paid within 15 days and enhanced for lower income tenants.
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units under RSO or JCO being demolished for new construction; Protected Units include units rent-restricted or rent-controlled within the past five years (all RSO units), units rented by lower or very low income households within the past five years, and units withdrawn under the Ellis Act within the past 10 years.
rules.exemptions: Regular RSO or JCO relocation rules apply if the units to be demolished are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation assistance and to file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental Housing Use with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) prior to evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
rules.interaction_text: Pay relocation assistance to tenants in compliance with the State law’s Housing Crisis Act (California Government Code Section 66300 et seq.) or the City laws, whichever is higher.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation requirements
rules.requirement: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict must comply with RPO relocation requirements, choosing one of 3 options and paying the highest applicable amount. Option 1 standardized payments for lower income households are $115,480 (extremely low), $96,750 (very low) and $87,450 (low income).
rules.key_value: Chart B: Extremely Low Income $115,480; Very Low Income $96,750; Low Income $87,450
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units demolished for the purpose of new construction.
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.quoted_span: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to comply with relocation requirements under the RPO. Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction_text: The owner must pay the highest of the applicable relocation amounts to comply with State and City laws.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower income households displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those required to be paid by public entities under Chapter 16 (commencing with Section 7260) of Division 7 of Title 1.
rules.coverage_text: Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced for demolition of units to be replaced with new construction.
rules.quoted_span: The City’s Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) and the State’s Housing Crisis Act (HCA) require that ONLY lower income households (80%  AMI or lower) being displaced for demolition of their units where the owner will replace the units with new construction receive relocation payment consistent to the relocation benefits required to be paid by public entities under Chapter 16 (commencing with Section 7260) of Division 7 of Title 1 (Government Code 66300.6(b)(4)(A)).
